title: Planning-to-delivery ownership
summary: Typed project and subproject planning, encrypted drafts and frozen workflow graphs share the existing execution ledger, isolated provider attempts, independent review and verified integration.

chapters.title: Planning and durable input
chapters.summary: Shared chat skins and the flow screen preserve device drafts before authenticated host mutation.

chapters.title: Frozen provider execution
chapters.summary: The approved baseline and exact role/model settings feed one SQLite execution ledger and managed attempt workspaces.

chapters.title: Review, integration, and preservation
chapters.summary: Exact result evidence gates integration; failed and interrupted attempts remain available, and portable restoration creates a separate project.

nodes.label: Flow screen and run results
nodes.detail: Subprojects and their flows share one project screen; a run's integration result and attempt evidence open in its result dialog.

evidence.claim: The flow screen opens a run's integration result and each attempt's evidence in one result dialog, and asks for an independent review again with one fixed command id per review round.
Diff, log and capture reads carry the flow's subproject, so a flow attempt's evidence is read in its own scope.

nodes.label: Shared bubble and CLI chat
nodes.detail: Both skins share one conversation. Draft handoff preserves input when history opens; command execution stays in the existing terminal path.

evidence.claim: One Session surface keeps its Session ID and transcript while skin selection changes presentation; the history control opens a separate picker.
Draft updates synchronously notify the owning form before a history action can unmount it, retaining the current provider, model, workspace, permissions and edited draft.
Both skins review only completed non-sensitive records from the selected session. Quotes enter the existing draft without submission; fragment records do not invent file line numbers.

nodes.label: Authenticated planning ingress
nodes.detail: Desktop surface identity and Android identity reach one host authority; legacy planning uses v13 and subproject workflow operations require v14.

evidence.claim: Planning reads/writes validate explicit subproject ownership and archive state before entering the existing readiness, trusted actor and local mutation boundaries.

Authenticated v14+ clients use workflow/capability handlers; v16-and-older readers get the reduced flow view and are marked for write protection; v13 keeps planning; subproject writes stay bound to the Android principal.

nodes.label: Project planning and baselines
nodes.detail: Explicit subprojects own independent planning files and immutable baselines that flow runs capture and restore imports; legacy planning stays bound to its default subproject.

evidence.claim: Flow runs capture baselines into the explicit subproject planning file, hashing the copied draft; an existing id must carry the same inputs, and the revision advances in the same atomic write.
Restore imports a planning snapshot only into a new project, checking every baseline hash and frozen reference before the first write.
The writer fsyncs a private temporary file, checks the expected disk hash and project boundary, then atomically renames.

nodes.label: Device encrypted recovery
nodes.detail: Drafts and exact pending commands survive restart with project/session identity and compare-and-swap; this is not transcript authority.

evidence.claim: Chat recovery requires authorized project/session scope, encryption availability, strict state validation, and the current recovery revision before an atomic encrypted write.
Flow graph recovery checks the host and project scope and the CAS revision, then writes the encrypted state atomically; it never replaces the saved flow.

nodes.label: Frozen execution preparation
nodes.detail: Explicit preparation resolves the approved baseline, task graph, allowed paths, exact models, inherited roles, and independent reviewer.

evidence.claim: Run commands, including a launch that prepares and starts one run and cancels it if its start is refused, freeze graph, baseline and auto-approve policy; agents cannot approve or integrate; the repeat schedule only launches.
Parent-to-leaf instructions and context values are frozen with exact provider/model/reasoning and read/write limits.

nodes.label: SQLite execution ledger
nodes.detail: The existing daemon database owns preparation, attempts, gates, artifact evidence, and revisioned command receipts.

evidence.claim: SQLite savepoints persist command identity, revisions and run state together; reads apply stage bindings over the verified preparation; new receipts and restart recoveries notify listeners after the write; it lists projects with runs.

nodes.label: Managed provider attempts
nodes.detail: Host scheduling creates isolated worktrees and environment leases, then sends frozen prompts through the existing provider runtime.

evidence.claim: Managed worktrees receive only accepted activations selected by the frozen graph, alongside deterministic attempt identity, environment leases and exact provider profile.
Submission includes frozen predecessor context; reconciliation records authoritative outcomes and captures partial artifacts without treating uncertainty as completion.

nodes.label: Captured result and review
nodes.detail: Host checks and a separate read-only reviewer bind findings to the exact baseline, artifact IDs, and validation plan.

evidence.claim: Result review retains exact artifact/baseline binding and an independent reviewer, with cancellation rechecked before each asynchronous validation/review boundary.
The reviewer output must identify the same baseline and artifact set; missing inspection evidence is recorded as not run.
User-attested device evidence is bound to the exact current attempt or integration candidate and a durable command identity; attempt evidence triggers a new independent review generation.

nodes.label: Verified integration candidate
nodes.detail: Only accepted artifacts are combined and checked; adoption compares the last successful ref and preserves the original checkout.

evidence.claim: Integration requires exact independently approved artifacts, validates the candidate, waits for its separate device evidence, and rechecks run revision before adoption.
Adoption requires a clean candidate and updates its dedicated integration ref only from the expected previous successful commit.

nodes.label: Portable archive and restore
nodes.detail: Export preserves planning/history evidence. Restore targets a new owned directory and retains historical execution without live permissions.

evidence.claim: Export persists a command intent and fingerprints its destination before producing the project archive.
Restore imports scoped planning and the workflow registry into a new project with 반복 off, retains session links as historical only, and rejects changed partial restores.

Planning edits (patch, freeze, branch, undo, profile proposals) are validated and refused since the planning screen was removed (I5); this path never changes the planning file.
